title: Exact inflation and invariants for product profinite condensed-group actions
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological groups), and write $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$, $\underline H(S)=C(S,H)$ for their condensed groups. For $P=1,G,H,G\times H$, let $\mathcal A_P(R)$ be the category of internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on this site equipped with an $R$-linear action $\underline P\times M\to M$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities, and equivariant $R$-linear morphisms. A linear action here means a family of module automorphisms parametrized by $\underline P$, or equivalently an action map additive and $R$-linear in the module variable. The trivial group gives ordinary internal $R$-modules.

These categories are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For the projections $G\to1$, $H\to1$ and $G\times H\to G$, inflation (give the kernel trivial action without changing the module or maps) is additive and exact and has the invariants under that kernel as additive right adjoint. Invariants are the submodule of sections fixed after every profinite base change: $m\in M(S)$ is invariant if for every $T\to S$ and $g\in C(T,\ker)$, $g\cdot m|_T=m|_T$. For $G\times H\to G$ this retains the induced $G$-action. The adjunction bijection sends a map from an inflated module to its same map with codomain restricted to invariants; its inverse composes the invariant-submodule inclusion. The inflation from $\mathcal A_1(R)$ to $\mathcal A_{G\times H}(R)$ is the composite of inflation to $G$ and then along $G\times H\to G$, and the conjugate right-adjoint comparison is the identity identification
$$M^{G\times H}=(M^H)^G.$$
These assertions include either group trivial and the zero ring. They concern actions of condensed groups, rather than actions of the abstract group on a discrete module.

proof.text: Put $C=*_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ in the size bound of the statement. Regard $R$ as its sheaf of commutative section rings. The tensor on abelian sheaves is the sheafified sectionwise tensor and abelian sheafification is strong monoidal by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Thus [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies: internal $R$-modules and sectionwise $R$-module sheaves are equivalent with precisely the same underlying sheaves and maps. A map $\underline P\times M\to M$ in the statement is exactly a family $C(S,P)\times M(S)\to M(S)$ natural in $S$; linearity and the action identities are the same sectionwise identities. Consequently this equivalence also identifies the categories with $P$-action. No discrete topology on a coefficient module has been introduced.

source.place: Paragraph (3), interpret the internal coefficient categories on the profinite site

proof.text: For each $P=1,G,H,G\times H$ apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] with $K(S)=C(S,P)$. Here $K$ is the condensed group $\underline P$ specified in the statement, with sectionwise multiplication and inverse; $C$ has finite limits and the prescribed covering families. The resulting $C_P$ is small in the fixed bound (each hom set is a set of pairs), and its ring $R_P$ is commutative. The cited equivalence identifies $\mathcal A_P(R)$ additively with $\operatorname{Mod}(R_P)$. Its kernel/cokernel assertion says that forgetting $P$ creates both; its zero-detection assertion also shows that underlying exactness detects equivariant exactness. Indeed homology is formed by kernels and cokernels, so it is zero exactly when its underlying module is zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), construct a small ringed-site presentation of the internal-action category

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] to the small site $C_P$ and the commutative ring sheaf $R_P$ just constructed. It supplies an abelian category with small colimits, exact filtered colimits and a generator. Carry these structures through the additive equivalence of step 2: universal properties give the transported kernels, cokernels and colimits, preservation of exactness follows from the transported kernels and cokernels, and the image of the displayed generator still detects different morphisms by full faithfulness. This proves that every $\mathcal A_P(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian. Neither nonzero coefficients nor a nontrivial group is required.

source.place: Section 07A5 (section-unbounded), opening paragraph: apply the ringed-site theorem to the site from step 2

proof.text: For a projection $\pi:P\to Q$ in the statement, define inflation by $p\cdot n=\pi(p)\cdot n$ on every section after every base change, and leave each linear map unchanged. Since $\pi$ preserves multiplication and identity this satisfies the action laws and respects equivariant maps. Addition is unchanged, so inflation is additive. By the kernel/cokernel formula of step 2, the inflated kernel and cokernel are precisely the kernel and cokernel of the inflated map: on the underlying sectionwise kernel or sheafified quotient the action is induced by the same formula $p\mapsto\pi(p)$. Thus inflation preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact.

source.place: Paragraph (3), exact inflation along the three split projections; direct argument from step 2

proof.text: Let $N=\ker\pi$. Define $M^N(S)$ by the quantified fixed-section condition in the statement. It is an $R(S)$-submodule since all $N(T)$ act linearly, and it is stable under restriction because the condition quantifies over every $T\to S$. It is a sheaf: glue a compatible invariant family in $M$; for $T\to S$ and $n\in N(T)$, pull the cover back to $T$ and compare $n\cdot m|_T$ with $m|_T$. They agree on this cover, hence agree in $M(T)$. In the product case $G$ acts by $(g,1)$ and preserves $M^H$ because $(1,h)(g,1)=(g,1)(1,h)$ on every base change. For a projection to $1$ no residual action remains. Restrict an equivariant map to these submodules; this defines the invariants functor. Restrictions of sums of maps are sums, so it is additive.

source.place: Paragraph (3), invariant subsheaf and its residual action, checked by gluing and commuting product factors

proof.text: An equivariant map $f:\operatorname{Inf}_\pi L\to M$ takes values in $M^N$: for $T\to S$, $n\in N(T)$ and $x\in L(S)$, one has $n\cdot f(x)|_T=f(n\cdot x|_T)=f(x|_T)$, since $N$ acts trivially on the inflated source. Thus the same section maps, with codomain restricted, define $\bar f:L\to M^N$. They are $Q$-equivariant: in the product case use the lift $(q,1)$; for $Q=1$ this condition is vacuous. Conversely compose a $Q$-equivariant map $L\to M^N$ with the inclusion. For $P=G\times H$, writing $(g,h)=(g,1)(1,h)$ proves equivariance since $h$ fixes its image; the projections to $1$ use the same fixed-image argument. The two constructions are inverse because the inclusions are injective on sections. Precomposition or postcomposition commutes with codomain restriction and inclusion, giving naturality in both variables. These are the asserted additive adjunctions with exactly the stipulated bijections.

source.place: Paragraph (3), construct and verify the inflation/invariants adjunction bijections

proof.text: Both inflations from $\mathcal A_1(R)$ to $\mathcal A_{G\times H}(R)$ leave the module and its maps unchanged and give every $(g,h)$ trivial action, so the direct and composite functors agree. For $m\in M(S)$, being fixed by all pairs after all $T\to S$ implies being fixed by $(g,1)$ and $(1,h)$. Conversely these two fixedness conditions give $(g,h)m=(g,1)(1,h)m=m$ on every such $T$. Therefore $M^{G\times H}$ and $(M^H)^G$ are the same submodule sheaf, naturally in $M$. Under the adjunction bijections of step 6, the direct and successive transposes of any map both retain its section maps and restrict their codomain to this same submodule. Hence the conjugate right-adjoint comparison is exactly this identity identification. When a group is trivial its fixedness condition is the unit law. When $R=0$ each unital section module is zero. The same constructions therefore include both stated edge cases.
